Notes
(a) Designated through-account; primary hub for inflows (direct deposit, Zelle and inbound transfers) and outflows (card payments, savings and reserve funding); swept as each paycheck is deployed, targeting a $100 operating balance.
(b) Designated reserve for rent and utilities; funded to $625 on the final pay cycle of each month, targeted to zero in between. Restricted cash.
(c) Designated reserve for the auto loan payment; funded to $490.70 on the final pay cycle of each month, targeted to zero in between. Restricted cash; bears interest at 3.44% APY.
(d) Reflected at cost, with adjustments as necessary to reflect material changes.
(e) Participates in Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP); shares purchased at 5% discount to market price at end of purchase period, recognized as income at purchase and reflected at cost.
(f) Excludes unvested equity awards, net of shares withheld for taxes, which are carried off balance sheet until vesting. Outstanding awards comprise 4 RSUs (BNY), cost basis $0.00 and fair value $575.48, inclusive of $4.64 of accrued dividend equivalents, vesting 2027-02-15; 6 shares of restricted stock (BNY), cost basis $451.86 and fair value $856.26, vesting 2027-11-01; aggregate cost basis $451.86 and aggregate fair value $1,431.74 as of the reporting date; recognized as income upon vesting.
(g) Net shared-expense balance with Hannah, presented as single current line; classified as current asset when in net receivable position and current liability when in net payable position.
(h) Designated reserve held in a high-yield savings account, available on demand and not restricted as to use; bears interest at an APY set 10 basis points below the lower bound of the federal funds target range. Funded toward a target of 75 days of monthly cash outflow, measured on the assumption that the support described below ceases. Certain recurring costs are borne by the reporting person’s parents and accordingly never enter these accounts — medical, dental, vision $350.00; therapy $250.00; cell phone service $100.00; gasoline $100.00 — aggregating $800.00 per month; a further $500.00 per month is received as a contribution toward the auto note and recognized in income.
(i) Carried at cost less accumulated depreciation, financed by auto loan payable; depreciated straight-line over 5 years, no salvage value.
(j) Represents reloadable, non-interest-bearing prepaid card used exclusively for parking at designated BNY Pittsburgh locations; non-redeemable and not convertible to cash; balance capped at $200.00.
(k) Revolving credit account (Discover It); purchases bear variable 16.49% APR; cash advances variable 28.49%; statement period runs from 17th through 16th of following month, with minimum payment due on 13th of each month, automatic payment scheduled on 11th.
(l) Revolving credit account (Bilt Blue Mastercard); purchases carry 10.00% promotional APR through ~Feb 2027, variable 31.74% thereafter; cash advances variable 31.74%; statement period runs 5th through 4th of following month, with minimum payment due on 27th of each month.
(m) Revolving credit account (Wells Fargo Autograph Visa Signature); purchases bear variable 27.74% APR; cash advances variable 27.49%; statement period closes late in the month, with minimum payment due on 20th of each month.
(n) Secured installment note on 2026 Kia K5 GT-Line (Fayetteville Kia of Fayetteville, NC); original principal $27,284.75 at fixed 2.99% APR; 60 monthly payments of $490.70 beginning Feb 9, 2026; finance charge computed daily; collateralized by the vehicle.
(o) Unsecured related-party note; original principal $3,000.00 at fixed 3.75% APR; 60 monthly payments of $54.99 beginning Jan 31, 2026, maturing Jan 1, 2031; prepayable without penalty, subject to minimum interest of 12.50.
(p) Cumulative net income retained; the earned component of net worth, exclusive of unrealized gains and losses carried in accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI).
(q) Cumulative unrealized gains and losses on investments carried at fair value; prior-period balances reflect lots currently held.

(h) Marcus
Designated reserve held in a high-yield savings account, available on demand and not restricted as to use; bears interest at an APY set 10 basis points below the lower bound of the federal funds target range. Funded toward a target of 75 days of monthly cash outflow, measured on the assumption that the support described below ceases. Certain recurring costs are borne by the reporting person’s parents and accordingly never enter these accounts — medical, dental, vision $350.00; therapy $250.00; cell phone service $100.00; gasoline $100.00 — aggregating $800.00 per month; a further $500.00 per month is received as a contribution toward the auto note and recognized in income.
(i) Vehicle – 2026 Kia K5 GT-Line
Carried at cost less accumulated depreciation, financed by auto loan payable; depreciated straight-line over 5 years, no salvage value.
(j) Value Card
Represents reloadable, non-interest-bearing prepaid card used exclusively for parking at designated BNY Pittsburgh locations; non-redeemable and not convertible to cash; balance capped at $200.00.
(k) Discover
Revolving credit account (Discover It); purchases bear variable 16.49% APR; cash advances variable 28.49%; statement period runs from 17th through 16th of following month, with minimum payment due on 13th of each month, automatic payment scheduled on 11th.
(l) Bilt
Revolving credit account (Bilt Blue Mastercard); purchases carry 10.00% promotional APR through ~Feb 2027, variable 31.74% thereafter; cash advances variable 31.74%; statement period runs 5th through 4th of following month, with minimum payment due on 27th of each month.
(m) Wells Fargo
Revolving credit account (Wells Fargo Autograph Visa Signature); purchases bear variable 27.74% APR; cash advances variable 27.49%; statement period closes late in the month, with minimum payment due on 20th of each month.
(n) Auto Loan Payable
Secured installment note on 2026 Kia K5 GT-Line (Fayetteville Kia of Fayetteville, NC); original principal $27,284.75 at fixed 2.99% APR; 60 monthly payments of $490.70 beginning Feb 9, 2026; finance charge computed daily; collateralized by the vehicle.
(o) Notes Payable (Mom)
Unsecured related-party note; original principal $3,000.00 at fixed 3.75% APR; 60 monthly payments of $54.99 beginning Jan 31, 2026, maturing Jan 1, 2031; prepayable without penalty, subject to minimum interest of 12.50.
(p) Retained Earnings
Cumulative net income retained; the earned component of net worth, exclusive of unrealized gains and losses carried in accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI).
(q) Accumulated other comprehensive income
Cumulative unrealized gains and losses on investments carried at fair value; prior-period balances reflect lots currently held.

Standing on
The contribution from Mom is ordinary cash — no principal-only paydown is proposed.
BNY is sold only to the size of a capital shortfall; the rest of the sleeve is held.
Only ESPP shares already on the books are considered at all.
Cash is never drawn below the 30-day runway limit to retire a revolver.
That reserve is sized on the burn he would carry unsubsidized, not the burn the ledger shows.
New investment dollars fill the Roth while contribution room remains, then taxable.
The monthly contribution from Mom is no longer earmarked to auto-loan principal; it is undesignated and may be deployed, including to Marcus.
An ESPP purchase settles before the 15th of each month — the incoming BNY shares are a known Tier 2 addition, never spendable cash.
ESPP shares arrive already concentrated in the employer, so trimming BNY takes priority over trimming a diversified holding.

Methodology. Sensitivities are exact recomputations at current levels, not linear approximations, so large movements can be read directly. Green indicates the movement improves the metric. Appetite buffers state the dollar movement in the numerator that would place the metric at its early warning threshold or limit. Dollar metrics (cash, debt, capital tiers) move one-for-one and are omitted. Joint-event rows recompute numerator and denominator simultaneously, since real transactions rarely touch one side alone.

north star · update
Deep space. Near-black violet ground with the circumpolar constellations at their true coordinates behind everything — Cassiopeia, the Little Dipper with Polaris at the end of its handle, and the Big Dipper below, its pointer stars aimed where they always point.

The mark. One eye is the Little Dipper with Polaris burning off the handle; the other is the circuit. Sky and machine, same owl.

Strategy is a terminal. A scrolling ratio tape that leads with whatever is binding, then Capital, Liquidity, Spending, Next dollar, Exposure and Signals. Every ratio shows its actual math — dollars over dollars — with its limit, early warning and target beneath it.

Next dollar, two ways. Toggle between the next paycheck and the book as it stands. Every move is priced by the app’s own engine and walked in sequence, so each step reads against what the prior steps left behind — Tier 1, leverage, runway, utilization, interest. Investing is the last claim and it names the gate that is blocking it.

Spending. Month to date against the trailing pace, every category broken into what it is made of, and a tap on any sparkline opens the full month history.

Reserves retired. No funded buckets, no banners. One operating floor on Wells Fargo; everything above it is deployable.

Auto loan. Payoff quote, per diem, next due, payments remaining and projected payoff — all ledger-driven at simple daily interest.

athena. She runs the whole app: accounts, configuration, subscriptions, loan payments, tabs. She checks precedent before booking anything recurring, reads capital tiers from the engine instead of guessing, ranks what to sell by goal rather than size, tracks Roth room by tax year, knows the ESPP lands before the 15th, and opens on a clean context every launch.
